baselineTriggers.B1_TREND_ADVERSE: close < mean of the last 200 closes (the existing overlay trend leg)
baselineTriggers.B2_VOL_ADVERSE: annualised vol63 > 25% (the existing overlay vol leg)
baselineTriggers.D10_TRAILING_DRAWDOWN: close / max of the last 252 closes - 1 <= -10%

cadence.FAST_MARKET_BREAK: daily state for event timing; weekly snapshots for statistical tables
cadence.SLOW_VULNERABILITY: monthly: last KR session of the month
cadence.TRANSITION_FINANCIAL_STRESS: weekly: last KR session of the week
cadence.slowerSeriesCarriedForward: latest KNOWN observation only; carried daily rows are never independent evidence

conceptualSequence: eventual future risk-budget decision (not this study)

drawdownEpisodes.algorithm: running peak P = the latest close >= every earlier close; a close >= P ends any open episode as a recovery and restarts the peak at that date; a close < P opens an episode (peak = the date P was last set) whose trough is the FIRST lowest close; depth = trough/peak-1; an episode open at the last observation is right-censored; missing sessions are skipped (episodes use observed closes only)

earlyDamage.slowWarnings: pre-peak lead time reported separately (active at peak with streak onset; on-then-off; never on); never mixed with a fast trigger
earlyDamage.triggerWindow: [peak, trough]; a state already on at the peak gives delay 0 and loss 0 and is flagged

existingOverlayReference.role: frozen BASELINE to measure, not the answer; reproduced exactly by a literal replica proven equal to state_at
existingOverlayReference.rule: close < mean of the last 200 closes; annualised vol63 > 25%; multipliers 1.0 / 0.7 / 0.4

perTrigger: share of ON (and OFF) sessions followed within H63/H126 by -10/-15/-20% worst loss
activation streaks with no -10% drawdown within H63
after each trough: sessions until the trigger's own off-state and the return missed meanwhile

fast_downside_vol_63.definition: sqrt(mean(min(r,0)^2)) over the last 63 returns x sqrt(252)

fast_drawdown_252.definition: minus (close / max of last 252 closes - 1), a depth >= 0

fast_overlay_count.definition: existing overlay: trend adverse (close < mean of last 200) + vol adverse (vol63 > 25%)

fast_realized_vol_21.definition: std (ddof 1) of the last 21 daily returns x sqrt(252)

fast_realized_vol_63.definition: std (ddof 1) of the last 63 daily returns x sqrt(252)

int_breadth_above_sma200.definition: minus fraction of PIT members above their SMA200

int_capweight_minus_equalweight_63.definition: cap-weighted minus equal-weighted 63-session return of PIT members (narrow leadership = risk)

int_concentration_top5_share.definition: top five signal-date market-cap share among PIT members

int_dispersion_63.definition: cross-sectional std of 63-session returns of PIT members

int_positive_breadth_63.definition: minus fraction of PIT members with a positive 63-session return

slow_fed_funds_change_126.definition: DFF(t) - DFF(t-126 sessions), percentage points (tightening = risk)

slow_inversion_duration_10y3m.definition: consecutive month-end observations with 10y-3m < 0 including t

slow_resteepening_flag_10y3m.definition: 1 if 10y-3m > 0 now and its minimum over the trailing 504 sessions was < 0, else 0

trans_benign_easing_flag.definition: easing, no 10y-3m inversion in the trailing 504 sessions, HY stress not worsening

trans_easing_after_inversion_flag.definition: easing with a 10y-3m inversion in the trailing 504 sessions

trans_post_vulnerability_stress_easing_h.definition: easing after inversion AND HY stress worsening (expanding percentile of HY level or 63-session change >= 0.75)

trans_post_vulnerability_stress_easing_v.definition: easing after inversion AND VIX stress worsening (expanding percentile of VIX level or 63-session change >= 0.75)

trans_usdkrw_realized_vol_21.definition: annualised std of the last 21 known log changes

hypotheses.H1: Yield-curve inversion / near-term policy-path weakness is primarily a slow vulnerability signal and should carry more information at H126/H252 than at H21.
hypotheses.H2: A policy-rate cut alone is not necessarily adverse; risk may be greater when easing follows prior curve vulnerability AND financial stress is worsening.
hypotheses.H3: Widening credit spreads / worsening external financial conditions contain transition information before or during large KR equity drawdowns.
hypotheses.H4: Fast trend/volatility deterioration may not predict the ultimate crisis in advance but may identify the early portion of a developing drawdown.
hypotheses.H5: The existing SMA200 + Vol63 overlay may reduce remaining drawdown, but its false-alarm and recovery-delay costs must be measured.
hypotheses.H6: KR market breadth/internal deterioration may add information beyond the index itself in the shorter PIT-safe extended sample.
hypotheses.H7: A slow-warning -> transition -> fast-break sequence may be economically more useful than any one signal; this study does not optimise or select a combination.
hypotheses.status: hypotheses, not truths; none is a result

lifecycle.executionLock: refs/tags/kr-market-risk-anatomy-v1-execution-lock plus -<specSha256>, atomic POST /git/refs; any existing ref refuses; failure before the lock spends nothing, after it consumes v1

limitations: One market time series with a handful of independent stress episodes: every statistic is descriptive and heavily autocorrelated
The sample is historically known to the researchers; a preregistration does not make it independent
Availability dates are conservative approximations; no release timestamps are retained, so no source is PIT_EXACT
A price index excludes dividends; drawdowns are price drawdowns, not shareholder total return
KR policy rate, KR term spread, Near-Term Forward Spread and the Excess Bond Premium are not available as defensible historical predictors
Extended internals start in 2015 and depend on the preserved raw input artifact
No multiplicity correction; no feature or trigger is validated or predictive

references: Estrella and Mishkin (1996, 1998): term spread and recessions
Engstrom and Sharpe (2019): near-term forward spread as a leading indicator
Federal Reserve staff work comparing term spreads and recession probabilities
Gilchrist and Zakrajsek (2012): credit spreads and business cycle fluctuations
Favara, Gilchrist, Lewis and Zakrajsek (2016): recession risk and the excess bond premium (EBP is revised modern data and is not used)
literatureMotivation.role: motivation only, never a result of this study

normalisation.invariance: the state at t is identical whether the data end at t or in 2026 (tested)

objective: Determine whether information observable at time t identifies elevated KR equity-market downside vulnerability and/or detects a developing large drawdown early enough to reduce a meaningful part of the remaining loss.

pitDiscipline.rule: a feature at KR session t sees the latest observation whose availableFrom (observation date + lag) is <= t

primaryReference.basis: PRICE INDEX LEVEL; never described as total shareholder return; the ETF robustness reference is the as-traded close, dividends not reinvested
freeze: calendar (XKRX sessions of the pinned repository calendar)
missing-date semantics (a missing session is missing; no fill)
primaryReference.rule: Walk the KOSPI 200 routes in REFERENCE_PRIORITY and take the first that passes every identity/coverage/semantics test; only if none passes may the KOSPI composite price index be chosen, and the decision says so. No splice, no silent substitution, never chosen on result quality.

vendorCrossCheck.effect: a CONFLICT against another route to the same index blocks the choice

coreGates.rule: READY only if the primary reference, at least one slow family, one transition family and one fast benchmark-derived family are covered in 2007-2009, and usable coverage exists around 2020; not every candidate feature must cover the period; each missing candidate keeps its own coverage table

readiness.failureReturns: DATA_BLOCKED_BEFORE_MARKET_RISK_ANATOMY with exact blockers; the study is never quietly redefined as 2015+
readiness.transitionGateFeatures: market-stress features only (HY/IG spread, VIX, USD/KRW); policy-only easing flags are tabulated but are not a gate

rolePriorityRule: the primary route unless it fails the weekly known-coverage gate in the 2007-2009 window; then the secondary; never both
scientificStatusMeaning: exploratory historical development on a market history that is already known
rules frozen before this study's formal outcome execution
not prospective confirmation, not validated, not predictive, not production-ready
preregistration and one-shot execution protect against post-outcome tuning inside this study; they do not make the sample independent
